sections.title: Nanofabrication and Nanocharacterization
sections.description: This course is intended for first year graduate students interested in the experimental practice of nanotechnology. In the context of a hands-on laboratory experience, students will gain familiarity with both top-down and bottom-up fabrication and characterization technologies. This will be achieved through the realization of a variety of micro- and nanoscale structures and devices that can exhibit either classical or quantum effects at the small scale. Although concepts relevant to the laboratories will be emphasized in lecture, it is expected that students will already have been exposed to many of the underlying theoretical concepts of nanotechnology in previous courses. Prerequisite: If course requirement not met, permission instructor required.

sections.title: Nanofabrication and Nanocharacterization
sections.description: This hands-on laboratory course provides students with direct access to the Quattrone Nanofabrication Facility (QNF) at the Singh Center for Nanotechnology. Students gain practical experience with both top-down and bottom-up nanofabrication techniques by fabricating a range of nanoscale devices and materials, including MEMS devices, directed self-assembly nanostructures, 2D graphene transistors, sensors, and CdSe quantum dots. Each student is assigned an individual wafer or chip and completes the full device fabrication process. Students receive hands-on training with nanofabrication techniques, including photolithography, electron beam lithography, laser lithography, reactive ion etching (RIE), inductively coupled plasma (ICP) etching, evaporation, sputtering, and plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition. Fabricated devices are characterized using advanced nanocharacterization tools, including optical and electron microscopy, reflectometry, profilometry, and probe stations. Permission from the instructor is required.
